clue.text: Two males wearing formal outfits for important meetings

indicators.note: what is worn sits on the outside, so one set of letters is clothed by the other

blocks.note: suits are formal outfits
M is the abbreviation for male, twice

explanation.surface: Two men put on their best suits before heading into a crucial meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' reads as the men having the suits on, and so it is cryptically too: the clothes go round the males.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a high-level conference between leaders, the top of diplomacy.

clue.text: American politician enthralled by science? This smells somewhat fishy …

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive inside its grip

blocks.note: SCI is a standard short form of science
A is the abbreviation for American
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A US politician dazzled by science, with a hint that something about it is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' usually means suspicious, but here it is literal: the dish does smell of seafood. The ellipsis invites that second look.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a seafood dish with a mild marine aroma.

clue.text: Second broadcast includes hot material

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the rest

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
to air something is to broadcast it
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A second broadcast featuring something hot, perhaps a spicy TV segment about fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric or yarn made from Angora goat hair, a textile.

clue.text: Provocative conclusion to column in popular church journal

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept
placed in something means set inside it

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
CE is the Church of England
the last letter of column
a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: A columnist ends their piece in a church magazine with an inflammatory flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England, a common crossword abbreviation; the final N of 'column' lodges inside the run of other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary remarks are inflammatory, designed to stir up anger, just as provocative ones are.

clue.text: Hairdressing business regularly seen in small towns?

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Hair salons are a regular feature of small-town high streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading sMaLl ToWnS from the first letter, every other letter spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is the establishment where a stylist cuts and styles customers' hair.

clue.text: Operations bringing in nothing after April by the way

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: APR is the calendar abbreviation for April
ops is short for operations
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Surgical operations make no money once April has passed, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after April' puts the month first, and 'by the way' is the definition, not a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is used to introduce an incidental remark, an aside, as 'incidentally' does.

clue.text: Wild animals run off, covered in little insects

indicators.note: something covered in another is wrapped all round by it

blocks.note: ants are small insects
to elope is to run off to marry secretly

explanation.surface: Wild animals bolt away, swarming with tiny ants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' is not a deletion signal here; it is a synonym for elope.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are fleet-footed horned grazing mammals of African and Asian plains.

clue.text: Short Instagram video is genuine, we’re told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that an Instagram clip is authentic, not faked.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL and REEL are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Instagram calls its brief vertical video clips Reels, a platform feature name.

clue.text: Quality land

blocks.note: first meaning: a characteristic or attribute
second meaning: real estate owned by someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality land' reads like praise for good farmland; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an attribute of something and an estate or holding of real estate.

clue.text: Officials set to transform administrative districts

indicators.note: to transform is to change form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
wards are electoral and administrative divisions of a city

explanation.surface: Officials are poised to overhaul the boundaries of local districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set to' looks like 'ready to'; in fact 'set' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are officials who supervise events such as races or concerts and keep order.

clue.text: Ace medical worker going round hospital when needed

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a doc is a doctor
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A first-rate medic does ward rounds at the hospital whenever called.
explanation.walkthrough: DOC goes round H to give DHOC, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this purpose', describing arrangements made as required rather than planned.

clue.text: Flexible item ruptured with holes

indicators.note: something ruptured is broken apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bendy object has split open and is now full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'item' and 'holes' go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a variant of lithe, meaning supple and bending easily, agile in body.

clue.text: Not playing around, sadly

indicators.note: around suggests messing about or being turned in every direction, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped fooling about and turned sorrowful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not playing around' reads as 'being serious'; the first two words are the fodder and 'around' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignantly means in a way that evokes keen sorrow or wistful regret, so touchingly sad.

clue.text: Somewhat wide-ranging segment of a recent Taylor Swift concert?

definitions.text: segment of a recent Taylor Swift concert?

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the hyphen of this compound

explanation.surface: A sprawling section of a Taylor Swift stadium show.
explanation.walkthrough: Taylor Swift's Eras Tour was built from sections, each devoted to one album period; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Each part of the Eras Tour show celebrated one phase of her career, an epoch.

clue.text: Chief component of phone containing metal

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the ringer is the part of a telephone that sounds
lead is a heavy metal

explanation.surface: The main part of a phone has a metal inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief component' looks like one phrase meaning the main part; 'Chief' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who leads a group, usually in mischief, its head or boss.

clue.text: Frustrated senior cops assigned to a job

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
appointed means given a post

explanation.surface: Senior police officers are irritated at being handed some task.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, Detective Inspector, is a British police rank; the plural gives the opening chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed and frustrated both describe the feeling when hopes or expectations are thwarted.

clue.text: Stone coming from blast area, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rock debris thrown out of a quarry blast zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a quarry; nine letters of 'blast area' rearrange into the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained translucent mineral, gypsum or calcite, carved for ornaments.

clue.text: Careless hit-and-run?

blocks.note: a slap is a hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver is the very picture of recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit-and-run' looks like one compound crime; split it and each word becomes a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and without proper attention, sloppy and hurried.

clue.text: Go too far on the subject of rearing dogs, perhaps

indicators.note: a rearing animal rises up on its hind legs, and in a down clue going upwards turns the letters back

blocks.note: as in arguing over something, about it
dogs are an example of pets, flagged by 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone takes their views on raising dogs a bit too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing' looks like raising animals, but in a down clue it means turning upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to exceed a limit, to go beyond what is acceptable.

clue.text: Fresh larvae, I guess, is a type of rich food

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively proposes fresh grubs as a delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I guess' sounds like a hedge, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver sausage is a soft spreadable pork liver product, heavy and fatty, so rich.

clue.text: Pictures of clubs in Eastern Massachusetts

blocks.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east
MA is the postal code for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Photographs of nightclubs on the eastern side of Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' reads as photos, but 'the pictures' is old British slang for the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures means going to see a film, so the place showing them.

clue.text: Method of cooking meat in edges of fire?

indicators.note: edges are the outermost parts, so only the first and last letters are kept
placed in something means set inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A way of cooking meat right at the edge of the flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a fair picture of the technique, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé food is doused in spirit and set alight, a dramatic culinary technique.

clue.text: Standard role in film getting cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so a letter is lopped off the end

blocks.note: an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: An ordinary film role ends up on the cutting-room floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter is dropped from the actor's role.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, as in 'up to par', an accepted norm.

clue.text: Animal rage freely flowing from execs

definitions.note: an adjective; 'from execs' means of or by executives

indicators.note: something flowing freely is loose and unconstrained, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bosses let loose a torrent of beastly fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tail phrase, adjectival in sense: something from executives is of management.
explanation.definitionFit: Managerial describes what belongs to or comes from managers, the executive tier of a company.

clue.text: Endlessly uses a loudspeaker to give someone grief

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: Tannoy is a public address system, used as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone harasses another by blaring at them over a loudhailer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is the British brand name for a public-address loudspeaker system, so 'tannoys' is to broadcast on one; both ends go.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: irritating or pestering a person causes them distress, the idiomatic sense of grief here.

clue.text: Piece in revolutionary multimedia issue

indicators.note: a piece is a fragment, so only part of the following word is taken
a revolution turns something round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the middle of this word

explanation.surface: An article in a radical multimedia publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a magazine edition, but it is a verb meaning to send out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as a chimney issues smoke.

clue.text: Area up front usually needs to house fruit machine

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only initials are kept
to house something is to give it a home inside

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
the first letters of these two words
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit machine needs placing in the front area of the venue, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit machine' is a British name for a slot machine; split apart, the fruit and the machine do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating mechanism, a robot or mechanical device.

clue.text: ‘Ideal’ days ultimately never materialise before noon

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letters are kept

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
the final letters of the two words
AM, ante meridiem, means before midday

explanation.surface: Perfect days never seem to arrive in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'days ultimately' tempts you to take the S; 'days' is just D, and 'ultimately' acts on the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, as in a dream home, it means perfect or the most wished for.

clue.text: Trendy person extremely precocious in their performing

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, the first and last
performing suggests acting up or doing tricks, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashionable type who was very advanced for their age when on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' is easy to skip as a filler word; its letters join the outer pair as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster follows the latest fashions and alternative trends, someone stylishly cool.

clue.text: It’s a typical measurement, of course

definitions.text: It’s a typical measurement, of course

blocks.note: surface reading: a standard or average size, nothing unusual
setter's reading: the length of a golf course, measured in units of three feet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally'; read literally it is a golf course, whose length is given in yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf holes and courses are listed by distance in yards, so their total length is the measurement.
